descriptionChirho: One's manner of life, habitual conduct, or pattern of behavior — the way a person lives and acts in society. Both singular and plural forms (including the single plural occurrence in Heb 13:7) denote the same semantic concept of lifestyle and ethical conduct. Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'conducta/conductas/manera de vivir,' Hindi 'आचरण' (ācaraṇ = conduct, behavior — same word for both clusters), Arabic 'سيرَة/سيرَتَكُم' (sīra = conduct, biography of behavior — same root س-ي-ر), Korean '행실/행위들' (haengsil = conduct / haengwi-deul = behaviors), Swahili 'mwenendo/maisha' (mwenendo = conduct, way of going / maisha = life, lifestyle). Used extensively in the Petrine and Pauline epistles to describe Christian ethical conduct (1 Pet 1:15, 18; 2:12; 3:1-2, 16; Gal 1:13; Eph 4:22; 1 Tim 4:12; Heb 13:7; Jas 3:13).
